title: Reasoning Pattern Quick Reference
tagline: Year 4 — Standard patterns and one-line methods for series, coding, ranking, directions, relations, arrangements and logic

introduction.overview: Reasoning questions fall into a small number of recurring patterns. This sheet lists them with a one-line method each: series (differences, ratios, squares), coding (shifts and positions), ranking (left + right − 1), direction (coordinates), blood relations (draw a tree), seating (anchors and chains; circular arrangements fix one person), syllogisms (Venn test), clocks (5.5° per minute) and calendars (odd days). Revision means recognising the pattern within seconds and applying its method.
introduction.placementRelevance: Pattern recognition is the quickest way to bank marks in the reasoning section.
introduction.realWorldContext: Recognising a familiar structure shortens any analysis.

learningObjectives: Recognise the pattern of a question
Recall the counting formulas for arrangements
Use the clock and calendar rules
Check with a quick sanity test

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Total = left rank + right rank − 1. Circular arrangements of n: (n − 1)!. Clock: relative speed 5.5° per minute.

coreDefinitions: Method: a standard way to solve a pattern.
Anchor: a clue that fixes a position.
Relative speed on a clock: 5.5° per minute.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: A reasoning question is a known shape in a new story.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Name the shape, recall the method, apply, sanity-check.

mainNarrative: In a row of 40, the 12th from the left is 29th from the right: 40 − 12 + 1.
Six people around a circular table can sit in 5! = 120 ways.
At 4:30 the hour hand is at 135° and the minute hand at 180°, so the angle is 45°; the formula gives |120 − 165| = 45°.
From a Monday, 18 days later is 18 mod 7 = 4 days ahead: Friday.
In a coding question, test a shift of +1, then +2, then position values.

deepDiveAspects.title: Syllogism quick test
deepDiveAspects.content: Draw circles and try to break the conclusion; if you can, it does not follow.

deepDiveAspects.title: Blood relations
deepDiveAspects.content: Draw a tree; use generation lines and sex symbols.

solvedExamples.title: Ranking
solvedExamples.question: A student is 12th from the left in a row of 40. Rank from the right?

solvedExamples.title: Circular
solvedExamples.question: In how many ways can 6 people sit around a round table?

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Recognise the pattern, recall its method, apply and sanity-check.

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: Reject answers that break a basic constraint.
placementTips.questionSelectionAdvice: Practise each pattern for a week.

selfCheckQuestions: Can I name a pattern quickly?
Can I use the clock rule?
